summary: Isle Royale NP lookout on Greenstone Ridge: steel tower assembled 1964 (41 ft 3 in), unstaffed after 1968, now a radio and air-monitoring site; tower room closed.

facts.design: U.S. Forest Service standard steel lookout tower with living quarters; angle steel on concrete piers; prefabricated cab about 14 by 14 feet
facts.agency: National Park Service (Isle Royale National Park)

access.note: Reached on foot by the Greenstone Ridge Trail or by boat to Daisy Farm Dock; the park says the tower room is closed, but visitors may climb partway up the stairs for views

visit.trail_note: Hike from Daisy Farm Campground or the Greenstone Ridge Trail; tower room closed, but visitors may climb partway up the stairs (climbable is false for the tower room only)

events.note: Greenstone Ridge Fire burned through part of the island soon after it became a national park. Wikipedia says the NPS responded with two 1939 towers; the nomination says the fire itself did not prompt them, but did inform where the first were placed
Wooden tower built at this spot. Wikipedia says the NPS built two towers; the nomination says CCC personnel built the earlier tower here with New Deal funds
Original wooden tower demolished (nomination) or torn down (Wikipedia)
Steel tower assembled July 1964 (nomination; it also says constructed June 1964). Wikipedia gives completion in 1965
By 1968 the tower was no longer staffed and was used to house the island's radio repeater; fire-management use declined after 1968
Radio repeater converted to solar power; non-historic storage shed added beneath the tower
Air-quality monitoring equipment installed at the tower
Added to the National Register of Historic Places, April 6, 2021

corrections.why: The NRHP nomination gives the tower as 41’-3” tall from the concrete piers, about 12.6 m. No page read gives 13.7 m.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Wikipedia's infobox says built 1964 and its text says completed 1965. The nomination says constructed June 1964 and assembled July 1964. The story gives the 1964 assembly and notes Wikipedia's 1965 completion date.
Wikipedia says the National Park Service constructed the 1939 towers. The nomination says NPS used New Deal funds and CCC personnel to build them. Both are reported.

Wikipedia says the NPS built the 1939 towers in response to the 1936 fire. The nomination says the fire itself did not prompt construction, since NPS already used lookouts as its strategy, but the fire did inform where the first towers were placed. Both are reported; the story does not pick one.

sources.title: Ojibway Fire Tower, National Register of Historic Places Nomination (NPS Form 10-900)

notes_for_editor: Brief's height 13.7 m is not in any page read. Corrected to 12.6 m from the NRHP nomination (41’-3” from the concrete piers). The npgallery.nps.gov asset page returned no text, so the nomination was taken from the npshistory.com PDF. Nomination gives both June 1964 construction and July 1964 assembly; Wikipedia gives 1964 in the infobox and 1965 for completion; all are kept. Wikipedia credits NPS with the 1939 towers; the nomination credits CCC personnel. Access: the NPS page says the tower room is closed but visitors may climb partway up the stairs; the story reports both and does not encourage climbing the tower. No photos added (no confirmed image URLs or licences). Nomination has many figures, not checked for licence. Verification 2026-10-09: the story's fire-cause claim was contradicted by the nomination and is now reported as a disagreement; 'in the cab' was removed (not in any page read); the 'scenic stop' and tower-room sentences were reworded so they no longer copy NPS wording.
